answer: Consider a bond-then-audit gate: each new agent locks a stake tied to capacity, so an identity can only wander into the market after paying full price. Newcomers cannot self-grade; a random panel of staked incumbents must review real work before the stake is refunded, and collusion is slashed to honest reviewers. A Sybil flood therefore faces a rising tide of locked capital plus audit throughput clones cannot fake. When the attacker's cost curve hits its zenith, mass identity farming turns ruinous rather than cheap.
